raw: {"analysis":"PHR provides a more structured and comprehensive delivery plan that addresses all repository constraints with specific operational detail. It correctly identifies the shared-config dual approval requirement, the VP of Engineering business-hours sign-off, the 24-hour code freeze on revert, the flaky network latency check handling, and the integration test cost/run limitations. CCL covers most of the same constraints but is less precise in some areas—for example, it suggests triggering integration tests on every push to the feature branch while also saying runs must be batched, creating ambiguity around the six-run daily limit. PHR also adds useful specifics like pre-requesting Jane Smith and Security Lead approvals to prevent bottlenecks, defining success criteria for probabilistic correlation (95% reconstruction), and pinning base SHAs for isolated worktrees. CCL's inclusion of a customer support validation step in staging is a nice operational touch that PHR lacks, and its rollback triggers (latency spikes, false positive rates) are more concrete than PHR's generic 'if production fails.' However, PHR's overall treatment of the constraints is more rigorous and actionable.","verdict":"PHR"}
